title: Induced Coherence in Quantum and Classical Interferometry: Origin and Control
authors: Balakrishnan Viswanathan, Ravi Kamal Pandey, Devendra Kumar Mishra, Sibasish Ghosh, Prasanta K. Panigrahi
abstract: The wave-particle duality that manifests in the Young's double-slit interferometry satisfying the well known Englert-Greenberger-Yasin inequality has recently been shown to obey a universal triality relation involving coherence, predictability and rather surprisingly entanglement. In the present work, we explicitly demonstrate the persistence of the triality relation in the quantum induced coherence interferometer and the classical configuration recovers the well known duality inequality. Furthermore, we explore the origin of coherence and entanglement, in the induced coherence interferometer, and means to control them. We show that path indistinguishability (or intrinsic indistinguishability of the sources) in our setup plays a complementary role in influencing both interference and entanglement. We bring out manifestly the nature of coherence in both classical and quantum versions of induced coherence interferometers.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes induced coherence in quantum interferometers, showing that the degree of interference, predictability, and entanglement are linked by a universal triality relation. The key finding is that coherence is fundamentally induced by achieving path indistinguishability between photon sources. This provides a quantitative understanding of the trade-off between these quantum properties.
main_problem: The paper investigates the origin and control of coherence and entanglement in interferometry, specifically demonstrating the persistence of a universal 'triality relation' involving coherence, predictability, and entanglement.
main_result: The authors prove that the triality relation ($V^2 + P^2 + C^2 = 1$) holds in the quantum induced coherence interferometer, showing that path indistinguishability is the key mechanism inducing coherence and entanglement.
method: The analysis uses quantum state formalism, deriving key observables like visibility (V), predictability (P), and concurrence (C) based on the overlap of idler photon paths.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum induced coherence interferometer utilizing two nonlinear crystals ($	ext{NL}_1, 	ext{NL}_2$) pumped by a weak laser to generate correlated photon pairs via SPDC.
important_parameters: Idler mode overlap/Transmission coefficient ($|T|$), background field mean photon number ($ ar{n}$), and the mixedness degree ($\eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the low-gain regime, assuming two-photon emission dominates, and later extends to mixed states.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the interferometer setup, showing the pumping of two crystals and the crucial alignment of the idler paths.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the quantum model and the triality relation in the low-gain regime. It then explores the role of idler alignment ($|T|$) and later extends the analysis to include background fields ($ ar{n}$) and mixed states ($\eta$).
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework connecting fundamental quantum concepts (coherence, entanglement, indistinguishability) to a measurable physical phenomenon (interferometry), which is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems.
